Phonology
Vowels
A, Ä, Á, E, É, Ë, I, Ï, Í, O, Ó, Ö, U, Ú, Ü, Y
Vowel values (approved Oct 20, 2026). One value per letter. In the pronunciation guides, "a" alone stands for Ä (cat) and "ah" for A.
A — /a/ — "ah", as in father
Á — /aː/ — long "aah"
E — /e/ — pure "eh/ay", like Spanish e
É — /eː/ — long "ay", as in they, with no glide
Ë — /ə/ — schwa "uh", as in about
Ä — /æ/ — "a", as in cat
I — /i/ — short "ee"
Í — /iː/ — long "ee"
Ï — /i/ — same sound as I, but it starts a new syllable after another vowel (no diphthong)
O — /o/ — pure "oh"
Ö — /ø/ — as in German schön
U — /u/ — "oo"
Ü — /ʉ/ — the vowel of Swedish hus
Y — /y/ — as in German für
Ó, Ú — (value not yet assigned; by the acute rule these would be long O and long U)
Vowel rules:
An acute accent (Á, É, Í) marks a long vowel.
Two dots on a, o or u (Ä, Ö, Ü) mark a fronted vowel.
Ë is always schwa.
Ï only marks a vowel that is pronounced separately from the vowel before it.
Stress always falls on the first syllable.
Consonants
B, C, Ç, D, F, G, H, J, K, L, M, N, Ñ, P, Q, R, S, T, V, W, X, Z
Affixes
Suffixes
-aast — indicating the highest degree of a quality or characteristic [est]
-id — Denotes a polite form or imperative
-s — Used to indicate the plural form of nouns. [s]
-rias — Denotes a rank or position
-ia — Can denote a quality or characteristic [ly]
-ön — Denotes a person or agent (Kälalön, Paröitön, Visalön, Kraugön)
-uis — Used to form the present participle of verbs [ing] (describing word); the verbal noun uses -adur (Teháladur, Mlusiuladur)
-ti — past tense (Finati, Eignti, Shadueti, Motaiti)
-ra — present tense (Eignra, Failra)
-laj — Used to form words that denote opposition, resistance, or contrast with something [less]
-ar — pluralization/collective noun formation
-niss — quality or state of being associated with the root word [ness]
-ijan — Used to denote affiliation or origin [ian]
-na — indicating an action or process related to the base word [en]
-ija — land of [ia]
-ür — Denotes a person or thing that performs the action of the verb or is associated with it [er]
-ipanste — Range of numbers between 10 and 20
-ven — tens (Duven = 20, Tyasven = 30)
-ema — ordinal numbers (Aitema, Kapema)
-ur — male (Könaiur, Futhur, Bredur)
-in — female (Könuin, Mothrin, Sekerin)
-gros — military person or title (Adelsgros, Kaucigros, Krügros)
-kommend — head of an institution (Hernäkommend, Pälontkommend)
-lend — land, homeland (Daihesilend, Heimalend, Mothrilend)
-os — past participle (tervos)
-adur — verbal noun [-ing] (Teháladur, Mlusiuladur)
Prefixes
Ze- — used to create adjectives indicating the absence or lack of a specific quality
Grammar
1. Word order
Subject - Verb - Object. Example: Vi parna (we stand); Ei Sjá ne (I see you).
Questions put the helping verb first: Kor'ne ...? (Do you ...?), Ueseta ...? (Is it ...?).
Adjectives come before the noun: Stön Rïkich (grand empire), Fölere Daihesilend (independent Daihesilend).
2. Articles
the = el (formal/scripture: Au). a = e. an = eu.
3. Pronouns
I = Ei | me = Ein | my = Nei | mine = einei
you = ne | your = nur | yours = Nurei
he = Han | him = Einur | his = Einti
she = Hona | her = Honti | hers = Hontei
it = Eta | its = Etati
we = vi | us = wein | our = eun | ours = Euni
they = tei | them = tá | their = tarön | theirs = Tarönei
who = tu
4. To be and helping verbs
am = jad | are = jeor | is = ues | was = var | were = Vari | be = ter | been = Terti
have = Eign | has = Eignra | had = Eignti
do = Kor | does = Kores | did = Jia
will (future) = bveinu | shall/should = Celja | can = uer | may = Má | might = Motes
5. Verb tenses
Present: stem + -ra (Eign > Eignra, Fail > Failra).
Past: stem + -ti (fina > Finati, Eign > Eignti, Shadue > Shadueti, Motait > Motaiti). A stem ending in -a usually drops it (Ahajka > Ahajkti, Cásta > Cásti).
Future: bveinu + verb (Vi'bveinu reröit = we will defend).
Participle "-ing" (describing): stem + -uis. Verbal noun "-ing": stem + -adur (Teháladur, Mlusiuladur).
Past participle: stem + -os (terve > tervos, begun).
Polite request / command: + -id (Grathid, Vinesid).
6. Nouns
Plural: -s after a vowel, -os after a consonant (säl > sälos, Trötinen > Trötinenos).
Words in -ön make their plural/group with -er (Kälalön > Kälaler).
Collective or abstract group: -ar (Monopanike > Monopanikar).
Male / female: -ur / -in (Könaiur / Könuin, Futhur / Mothrin, Impëretur / Impëretin).
Person who does something: -ön (Paröitön, Visalön). Military person or title: -gros (Adelsgros, Krügros). Rank: -rias. Head of an institution: -kommend.
Land of: -ija (Morkavija); homeland / land: -lend (Daihesilend, Heimalend). People of: -ijan.
7. Adjectives and adverbs
Adjective from a noun: + -i (Bépode > Bépodi, Astár > Astáli, Kürmrahe > Kürmrahi).
Comparative: -ar/-ra (Bevitre > Bevitrar, Betra). Superlative: -aast.
Adverb (-ly): -ia. Quality (-ness): -niss. Without (-less): -laj (eud > Eudlaj).
Lacking: Ze-. Again/re-: Zá- (Zácekape). Un-/in-: En- (Enrettléti, Enfurl).
8. Negation
no = nöl. not = nölki, placed after the verb: Ei jad nölki ... (I am not ...).
In contractions it shortens to -lki after a vowel (Jia + nölki = Jialki) and 'nol after a consonant (uer'nol).
9. Contractions
Pronoun + helping verb: pronoun'verb (Ei'jad, Vi'jeor, Tei'bveinu, Kor'ne).
Preposition + the (el): joined (ol > Ole, et > Ete, uen > Uenel, ues > Uesel, täl > tel, uor > uoreli).
Preposition + a (e): joined (uen > Uene). Preposition + our (eun): joined (Eteun, Ueseu, Sieun).
10. Numbers
Units: Saei 0, Une 1, Dua 2, Tyas 3, Rouon 4, Daune 5, Syen 6, Tysa 7, Ait 8, Niye 9, Kap 10.
Teens: unit + -ipanste (Uneipanste 11, Duaipanste 12, Aitipanste 18).
Tens: unit + -ven (Duven 20, Tyasven 30, Rouonven 40, Dauneven 50, Syenven 60, Tysaven 70, Aitven 80, Niyeven 90).
In between: tens + und + unit (Duven und Ait = 28). Hundred = Hundrë, Thousand = Tüsen, Million = Millien.

Ordinals: unit + -ema, a final -e drops (Tyasema, Rouonema, Daunema, Syenema, Tysaema, Aitema, Niyema, Kapema). First = Fosunemer and Second = Düemer stay irregular, like English first/second. For bigger numbers add -ema to the last part (Duvenema 20th).
Ordinal abbreviations: 1st = 1er, 2nd = 2en, 3rd = 3e, 4th = 4a, 5th = 5a, 6th = 6a, 7th = 7a, 8th = 8a, 9th = 9a, 10th = 10a (endings: st = er, nd = en, rd = e, th = a).
Vocabulary
A
Abete (ah-beh-teh) (adjective, past participle) Having departed or disappeared; no longer present, existing, or accessible. — English: Gone, Departed, Lost
Adelsa (ah-dehl-sah) (noun) Referring to the whole or entirety of something; encompassing all aspects or elements. — English: General - overall, whole
Adelsgros (ah-dehl-sgrohss) (noun) A high-ranking military officer, typically one with authority over a group of soldiers or commanders. — English: General - military officer
Aerïcer (ah-eh-ree-kehr) (verb) To arrive at or get as far as a place, goal or person; to stretch out toward something. — English: Reach
Aganet (ah-gah-neht) (noun) The state of being joined together as one; oneness and agreement among people. — English: Unity
Agante (ah-gahn-teh) (verb) To join together into one; to bring or come together for a shared purpose. — English: Unite
Agantid (ah-gahn-teed) (adjective) Joined together into one; acting together as a single body. — English: United
Age (ayj) (noun) The length of time a person or thing has existed; the period of life characterized by certain stages of development. (verb) To grow older or more mature over time. — English: Age
Agüst (ah-güst) (proper noun) The eighth month of the year. — English: August
Ahajka (ah-hahy-kah) (verb, adjective) To stop sleeping; (adjective) not asleep, alert. — English: Awake
Ahajkanti (ah-hahy-kahn-tee) (adjective, past participle) Having been woken; roused from sleep or from a passive state. — English: Awakened
Ahajkti (ah-hahy-ktee) (verb (past)) Past tense of Ahajka; stopped sleeping, woke up. — English: Awoke
Ahal (ah-hahl) (noun) A system of rules or principles that govern behavior, often established by a governing body or authority. — English: Law
Áhyggia (aah-hy-gee-ah) (verb, noun) To be troubled about what may happen; (noun) a worry. — English: Worry
Ait (ay-it) (numeral) The cardinal number representing the quantity of eight; one more than seven, one less than nine. — English: Eight
Aitema (ay-it-eh-mah) (numeral) The ordinal number that marks the position of something as number eight in a sequence. — English: Eighth
Aitipanste (ay-it-ee-pan-steh) (numeral) The cardinal number representing the quantity of eighteen; the result of adding eight to ten. — English: Eighteen
Aitven (ait-vehn) (numeral) The cardinal number eighty; eight times ten (Ait + -ven). — English: Eighty
Akir (ah-keer) (verb) To emerge from sleep or unconsciousness; to become alert or conscious again. — English: Wake
Ákveda (aahk-veh-dah) (verb) To make up one's mind. — English: Decide
Ales (ah-les) (verb) To offer, present, or hand something to someone. — English: Give
Aleyues (ah-leh-yoo-ess) (verb) To set free, let go, or discharge something or someone from restraint or confinement. — English: Release
Alfuthur (ahl-foo-thoor) (noun) The father of one’s parent; a respected, elderly man, often a patriarch in a family. — English: Grandfather
Allt (ahlt) (pronoun) The entirety or whole of something; every part or individual element. (adjective) Describing the whole or complete amount of something. — English: All

Alolazgloire (ah-loh-lahz-glwah-reh) (noun, verb) (noun) A heartfelt expression of admiration or worship, often accompanied by gratitude or devotion. (verb) To praise, honor, or show deep appreciation for someone or something. — English: Praise
Álskad (aahl-skahd) (adjective) Deeply loved or cherished; held in great affection or esteem. — English: Dear, Beloved
Alvius (ahl-vee-oos) (adverb) At all times; without interruption or change, continuously. — English: Always
Amumin (ah-moo-meen) (noun) The mother of one’s parent; a respected, elderly woman, often a matriarch in a family. — English: Grandmother
Anda (ahn-dah) (verb) To take air into the body and let it out (from Ando). — English: Breathe
Andekaer (ahn-deh-kah-ehr) (noun) A war without end; a conflict that is thought to last forever. — English: Eternal War
Andelaus (ahn-deh-lowss) (noun) The infinite or timeless duration, beyond the scope of human life or understanding; endless existence. — English: Eternity
Andelo (ahn-deh-loh) (adjective) Lasting forever, without end or change; timeless and perpetual. — English: Eternal

Añdlit (ahn-dlee-t) (noun) The front part of the head, including the eyes, nose, and mouth; the expression or appearance of a person’s face. (noun) A surface or outward appearance representing identity or emotion. — English: Face
Ando (ahn-doh) (noun) The act or process of inhaling and exhaling air, sustaining life; a vital sign of existence. — English: Breath
Anecepte (ah-neh-kehp-teh) (verb, noun) To shape metal by heating and hammering; to create something with effort. (noun) A smithy or furnace for working metal. — English: Forge
Aneteporen (ah-neh-teh-poh-rehn) (interjection, noun) A parting word said when someone leaves for a long time; a goodbye. Also written Aney-Teporen. — English: Farewell
Aney-Teporen (ah-nay-teh-poh-rehn) (interjection, noun) Variant spelling of Aneteporen; a parting word, farewell. — English: Farewell
Animitra (ah-nee-mee-trah) (noun) The person in charge or leader of a group, organization, or community; one who holds a prominent or guiding role. — English: Head
Antasol (ahn-tah-sohl) (noun) The time that is still to come. Short form of Antasolizáspariesimeyni. — English: Future
Antasolizáspariesimeyni (ahn-tah-soh-lee-zaahs-pah-ree-eh-see-may-nee) (noun) The time that is still to come; what will happen later. Full form; the short form is Antasol. — English: Future
Anthäma (ahn-tha-mah) (noun) A formal song or composition, often associated with patriotism or ceremonial events. — English: Anthem
Aprél (ah-prayl) (proper noun) The fourth month of the year. — English: April
Arë (ah-ruh) (noun) A distinct period or age in time, often defined by significant events, changes, or cycles in history or culture. — English: Era
aredeácet (ah-reh-deh-aah-keht) (noun) A public or formal statement that makes something known. — English: Announcement
Arna (ahr-nah) (adverb) In this location; at or in the present place. — English: Here
Arnad (ahr-nahd) (adjective) Carrying weapons; equipped for fighting. — English: Armed
Artäla (ahr-ta-lah) (noun) A system of government where a single person, the monarch, holds supreme authority, often passed down through hereditary lines. — English: Monarchy

Artälön (ahr-ta-lön) (noun) A person who supports or advocates for a system of government in which a monarch holds power. (adjective) Relating to or supporting monarchy as a form of government. — English: Monarchist
Ásta (aahs-tah) (noun) A deep, enduring feeling of affection, passion, and attachment toward someone or something. — English: Love
Astáli (ahs-taah-lee) (adjective) Pleasing to the eye; having qualities that evoke admiration or delight. — English: Beautiful
Ástana (aahs-tah-nah) (verb) To feel deep affection and attachment toward someone or something (Ásta + -na). — English: Love
Ástanti (aahs-tahn-tee) (verb, past) Felt love for; past tense of Ástana. — English: Loved
Astár (ahs-taahr) (noun) The quality of being visually or aesthetically pleasing; an admired and graceful appearance or form. — English: Beauty
Au (ow) (article) Another word for "the", typically used in scriptures and formal writing. — English: The (formal, scriptural)
Auratetien (ow-rah-teh-tee-ehn) (noun) The power or right to give orders and make decisions; a person or body that holds such power. — English: Authority
Auratetinön (ow-rah-teh-tee-nön) (noun, adjective) A person who demands strict obedience to authority; (adjective) favoring strict obedience to authority. — English: Authoritarian
Auratetinonism (ow-rah-teh-tee-noh-neesm) (noun) A system or belief that favors strict obedience to authority at the cost of personal freedom. — English: Authoritarianism
Aust (owst) (noun) The direction toward the rising sun; associated with the point of the compass where the sun rises. (verb) To move or orient toward the east. — English: East
Austën (ow-stuhn) (adjective) Of or relating to the east; situated or located in the direction of the rising sun. — English: Eastern
Avar (ah-vahr) (adverb) At any time; at all times. As in Fer'avar (forever). — English: Ever
Averei (ah-veh-ray) (adverb) One more time; once more. — English: Again
Avereila (ah-veh-ray-lah) (preposition) In opposition to; in contact with or leaning on. — English: Against
Ävöxt (a-vökst) (noun) The sweet part of a plant that holds the seeds and can be eaten. — English: Fruit
Ayasicht (ah-yah-seekht) (adjective) Very large, important or excellent; of high quality or rank. — English: Great
B
Baipastete (bai-pahs-teh-teh) (noun) The word or words by which a person, place or thing is known. — English: Name
Baja (bah-yah) (noun) The rear part or opposite side of something; a position behind or reverse of the front. — English: Back
Bajan (bah-yahn) (preposition, adverb) At or toward the back of something; after or later than (Baja + -n). — English: Behind
Báles (baah-lehs) (verb) To ask divine favor for someone or something; to make holy. — English: Bless
Bänte (ban-teh) (noun) A person who has recently joined a group, especially in a military or organizational context, and is undergoing initial training. — English: Recruit
Bäntegros (ban-teh-grohs) (noun) A unique military rank. — English: Unique rank
Bära (ba-rah) (verb) To hold and take something from one place to another. — English: Carry
Bäta (ba-tah) (verb) To make something broken work again. — English: Repair, Fix
Beat (beet) (verb) To strike repeatedly with force or effort; to overcome or surpass in competition or difficulty. — English: Beat
Bein (bayn) (noun) One of the hard parts that form the skeleton. — English: Bone
Belëde (beh-luh-deh) (noun) A color resembling the clear sky or deep sea; often associated with calmness, depth, and serenity. — English: Blue
Béllac (bay-lahk) (adjective) Pertaining to or associated with a monarchy, nobility, or royal family; having the qualities or status of royalty. — English: Royal
Bellés (beh-layss) (adverb) Used to emphasize the extent or degree of something; to a high degree or intensity. — English: Very
Belluñ (beh-loon) (noun) A person belonging to a community or nation, typically one not engaged in military service; a member of the civil population. — English: Civilian / Citizen
Belluñ-Ovreorön (beh-loon-oh-vreh-oh-rön) (noun) An official who oversees local issues in smaller subdivisions. — English: Local overseer (smaller subdivisions)
Belóne (beh-loh-neh) (noun) The blossoming or flourishing of a flower, plant, or idea; the moment of full unfolding or growth. — English: Bloom
Bënke (buhn-keh) (noun) A color that is the darkest shade, the complete absence of light; often symbolizing mystery, depth, or formality. — English: Black
Bépode (bay-poh-deh) (noun) The red liquid that circulates through the veins and arteries of humans and animals, vital for life and carrying oxygen and nutrients. — English: Blood
Bépodi (bay-poh-dee) (adjective) Covered or stained with blood; associated with violence, injury, or bloodshed. — English: Bloody
Beräg (beh-rag) (verb) To boast or speak proudly about one’s achievements, qualities, or possessions, often to an excessive or arrogant degree. — English: Brag
Bërenadigros (buh-reh-nah-dee-grohs) (noun) A unique military rank. — English: Unique rank
Berguröna (behr-goo-rö-nah) (noun) A place where alcoholic beverages are served, often accompanied by food and entertainment; a tavern or pub. — English: Bar
Berijece (beh-ree-yeh-keh) (noun) A structure built over a river, road or gap so people can cross. — English: Bridge
Betra (beh-trah) (adjective) Of a higher quality, more desirable, or more effective than something else; superior in comparison. — English: Better
Bevitrar (beh-vee-trahr) (adjective) More luminous or radiant than something else; characterized by greater brightness or light. — English: Brighter
Bevitre (beh-vee-treh) (adjective) Emitting a strong, vivid light; full of light or brilliance; radiant. — English: Bright
Bëyene (buh-yeh-neh) (noun) A warm, earthy color often resembling soil, wood, or autumn leaves; associated with stability and naturalness. — English: Brown
Bída (bee-dah) (verb) To stay where one is until something happens. — English: Wait
Bitra (bee-trah) (adjective) Having a sharp, unpleasant taste. — English: Bitter
Björa (byö-rah) (noun) A drink made from grain. — English: Beer
Böca (bö-kah) (noun) A set of written or printed pages, typically bound together, containing text, images, or both, and usually used for reading or reference. — English: Book
Bolli (boh-lee) (noun) A small bowl-shaped container for drinking from. — English: Cup
Bolungros (boh-loon-grohs) (noun) A unique military rank. — English: Unique rank
Bonselar (bohn-seh-lahr) (verb) To separate into pieces or stop functioning temporarily; to interrupt an activity or process. — English: Break
Bord (bohrd) (noun) A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs. — English: Table
Bosäta (boh-sa-tah) (verb) To speak with excessive pride about one's accomplishments or possessions, often to impress others. — English: Boast
Bovutegloire (boh-voo-teh-glwah-reh) (adjective) Showing courage and determination in the face of danger or adversity; displaying boldness and valor. — English: Brave
Bredur (breh-doohr) (noun) A male sibling; a person who shares at least one biological or familial parent with another individual. — English: Brother
Breide (bray-deh) (adjective) Large from side to side; broad. — English: Wide
Brenna (breh-nah) (verb) To be on fire or to set on fire; to destroy or damage with fire or heat. — English: Burn
Breyta (bray-tah) (verb) To make or become different. — English: Change
Brjöst (bryöst) (noun) The front of the body between the neck and the stomach. — English: Chest
Bröd (bröd) (noun) A food made from flour and water, baked in an oven. — English: Bread
Brosa (broh-sah) (verb, noun) To curve the lips upward in pleasure; (noun) a smile. — English: Smile
Buaionn (boo-ah-ohn) (adjective) Tied or secured together; having a fixed connection or limitation. — English: Bound

Bveinu (bvay-noo) (noun, helping verb) The inner drive or determination that directs actions and choices; a personal force of intention or decision. Also the future helping verb: Vi'bveinu = we will. — English: Will
C
Cälendija (ka-lehn-dee-yah) (proper noun) The nation of Lengeria. — English: Lengeria
Calueti (kah-loo-eh-tee) (verb, adjective) To shut; to move something so that it covers an opening. (adjective) Shut; near. — English: Close
Cámilemä (kaah-mee-leh-ma) (numeral) Fifth; the ordinal for five. Old form; the standard form is now Daunema. — English: Fifth (old form)
Carae (kah-rah-eh) (verb) To go away from a place or person. — English: Leave
Cásta (kaahs-tah) (verb, noun) To touch with the lips as a sign of love or greeting; (noun) such a touch. — English: Kiss
Cásti (kaahs-tee) (verb (past)) Past tense of Cásta; touched with the lips. — English: Kissed
Caugra (kow-grah) (noun) The ability to face danger, pain or fear without giving in. — English: Courage
Cebret (keh-breht) (preposition, adverb) On the subject of; concerning. (adverb) Approximately. — English: About
Ceçesi (keh-seh-see) (noun) A series of connected metal rings. — English: Chain
Cekape (keh-kah-peh) (verb) To make something by putting parts together; to bring something into being. — English: Build / create
Cekapi (keh-kah-pee) (noun) A person or being who makes or brings something into being. — English: Creator
Celja (kehl-yah) (helping verb) Used to express what will happen or what ought to happen. — English: Shall / should
cepöne (keh-pö-neh) (verb, noun) To act violently against someone or something; (noun) an act of attacking. — English: Attack
Cept (kehpt) (verb) To have or hold onto something; to continue doing something. — English: Keep

Ceun (koyn) (noun) A period of sixty minutes. — English: Hour

Coratetale (koh-rah-teh-tah-leh) (adjective) Relating to correction or to the reform of offenders. — English: Correctional

Cöuncilos (kö-oon-kee-lohs) (noun) A group of people chosen to advise, govern or decide. Also Cöuncila. — English: Council
Cuinet (koo-ee-neht) (adjective) At or near the middle; most important; main. — English: Central
Cuinetekommend (koo-ee-neh-teh-koh-mehnd) (noun) The head of the Military Perauoamle. — English: Head of the Military Perauoamle

Cypörenija (ky-pö-reh-nee-yah) (proper noun) The nation of Laporannia. — English: Laporannia
D
